frozen_hypothesis: Files present but undeclared, and declarations without hashes, are both manifest gaps and both detectable.
frozen_required_deliverable: Bidirectional manifest gap detection reporting undeclared-present and declared-unhashed entries separately.
po01_contact_check: READ-ONLY CONFIRMED. I materialised the real pack into scratch with 'git archive <pinned sha> packs/repository-engineering | tar -x', which cannot mutate the source. All my mutated copies were made under scratch, never under packs/**.

synthetic_evidence_assessment.finding: This unit is the most synthetic-only of the three pack-gap units I reviewed. Unlike units 017 and 018, manifest_gaps.py has NO pinned-commit code path at all - it accepts only --pack-dir over a filesystem directory - and the producer's entire committed evidence is one invented fixture. The producer never touched the real pinned pack.
synthetic_evidence_assessment.does_the_synthetic_case_stand_in_for_the: In this instance, YES - but only because I checked, and the producer did not. I materialised the real pinned pack and ran the detector against it directly (HC-A), then derived positive cases from the real pack rather than from an invented one (HC-B, HC-B2). The component generalises correctly. So here the synthetic-only evidence UNDERSTATES a component that actually works on real input, which is the opposite of the usual risk. That is still a reporting deficiency: nothing in the producer's committed evidence would have told a reader this.

hidden_cases.rationale: The producer never ran the detector against the real pinned pack. Since the frozen hypothesis is about manifest gaps in operator packs, that is the population that matters.
hidden_cases.construction: git archive 1e6f53c323f8326d12af213557082a3665991f19 packs/repository-engineering | tar -x, then python3 -I manifest_gaps.py --pack-dir <real pack> --manifest MANIFEST.json
hidden_cases.interpretation: The detector works on the real pack and finds it clean: 8 declared, 8 present, no undeclared files, no unhashed declarations. The real pack directory contains exactly BOUNDARIES.md, LAUNCH.md, MANIFEST.json, checks.py, engine.py, oracle.py, state_machine.py, test_pack.py and transport.py - 8 files plus the manifest itself, which the detector correctly excludes from the present set.

hidden_cases.rationale: Detection-power probe derived from the REAL pack rather than an invented fixture, which is a stronger positive case than the producer's.
hidden_cases.construction: Copy of the real pinned pack with one extra undeclared file 'smuggled_payload.py' added.
hidden_cases.interpretation: Correctly fires on real-pack-derived input, names the smuggled file, and reports it in the undeclared_present channel rather than conflating it with the unhashed channel.

hidden_cases.rationale: The obvious way to hide an undeclared file is to bury it in a subdirectory. The producer's flat fixture cannot test this.
hidden_cases.construction: Copy of the real pinned pack with 'internal/hidden.py' added in a new subdirectory.
hidden_cases.interpretation: Caught, with the correct posix-relative path. rglob('*') plus relative_to() means nesting is not an escape route.

hidden_cases.rationale: declared_unhashed is computed as 'not metadata.get("sha256")', a truthiness test. Any non-empty string therefore counts as a hash, including a placeholder.
hidden_cases.construction: Copy of the real pinned pack with BOUNDARIES.md's declared sha256 replaced by the literal string 'TBD'.
hidden_cases.interpretation: GAP. A declaration carrying 'TBD' instead of a hash is reported as fully hashed and the pack passes. Under the frozen hypothesis this is a declaration without a hash, and it is not detected. No format or length validation is applied to the declared value.

hidden_cases.rationale: Control for HC-D, to confirm the unhashed channel works at all when the key is genuinely absent.
hidden_cases.construction: Same copy with the sha256 key deleted rather than replaced.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-D2 control, sha256 key deleted on BOUNDARIES.md: {"declared_unhashed": ["BOUNDARIES.md"], "verdict": "FAIL"}
hidden_cases.interpretation: Correctly detected. This isolates HC-D precisely: the channel works for a missing key and fails only for a present-but-meaningless value.

producer_declared_limitations: This unit isolates manifest coverage categories and does not claim that a self-hashing manifest is possible.
scope_honesty_assessment.assessment: The declared limitation is technically true but essentially unrelated to the interesting risks. The two things a reader needs to know are undeclared: that the component has no pinned-commit path and was never exercised against a real pack, and that the declared-unhashed channel is a truthiness test that a placeholder value defeats. To the producer's credit, the fixture files are all listed in the manifest with hashes and byte counts, and the fixture carries an explicit SYNTHETIC_..._FIXTURE label so it cannot be mistaken for real pack data.

reproducibility_check: All five cases were run in fresh python3 -I processes against a pinned git-archive export; results reproduced on repeat.
disposition_reason: ACCEPTED because both directions the frozen deliverable names are genuinely implemented and reported in separate channels, and I confirmed them on real-pack-derived input rather than on the producer's fixture: a smuggled undeclared file is caught by name, an undeclared file buried in a subdirectory is caught with its correct relative path, and a deleted sha256 key is caught in the unhashed channel. Against the real pinned pack the detector reports it clean, 8 declared and 8 present. Two things I would have the coordinator note. First, the placeholder-hash gap (HC-D): a declaration whose sha256 is the literal 'TBD' is reported as hashed and passes, which is arguably a declaration without a hash going undetected - a hardening item rather than grounds for rejection, since the missing-key case is correctly caught. Second, this is the only one of the three pack units with no pinned-commit code path and no real-pack evidence at all; here that understated a component that actually works, but the coordinator should not rely on that being true in general.
followups_for_coordinator: declared_unhashed uses 'not metadata.get("sha256")', a truthiness test. Reviewer-observed: replacing a real hash with the literal string 'TBD' yields declared_unhashed=[] and verdict PASS, while deleting the key yields the correct FAIL. Validate the declared value as 64 lowercase hex characters instead of merely non-empty.

Add a pinned-commit code path (as units 017 and 018 have) and record at least one real-pack run in the evidence. The component already works on the real pack - I verified 8 declared / 8 present / no gaps - but no committed evidence shows it.
